question: In the “olist_geolocation” table, please identify which two consecutive cities, when sorted by geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, and geolocation_lng, have the greatest distance between them based on the difference in distance computed between each city and its immediate predecessor in that ordering.
sql:
WITH ordered_rows AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    geolocation_state,
    geolocation_city,
    geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
    geolocation_lat,
    geolocation_lng
  FROM olist_geolocation
),
numbered AS (
  SELECT
    geolocation_state,
    geolocation_city,
    geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
    geolocation_lat,
    geolocation_lng,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng
    ) AS rn
  FROM ordered_rows
),
consecutive AS (
  SELECT
    prev.geolocation_state AS state1,
    prev.geolocation_city AS city1,
    prev.geolocation_zip_code_prefix AS zip1,
    prev.geolocation_lat AS lat1,
    prev.geolocation_lng AS lng1,
    curr.geolocation_state AS state2,
    curr.geolocation_city AS city2,
    curr.geolocation_zip_code_prefix AS zip2,
    curr.geolocation_lat AS lat2,
    curr.geolocation_lng AS lng2,
    6371 * ACOS(
      GREATEST(-1, LEAST(1,
        COS(RADIANS(prev.geolocation_lat)) * COS(RADIANS(curr.geolocation_lat)) *
        COS(RADIANS(curr.geolocation_lng) - RADIANS(prev.geolocation_lng)) +
        SIN(RADIANS(prev.geolocation_lat)) * SIN(RADIANS(curr.geolocation_lat))
      ))
    ) AS distance_km
  FROM numbered curr
  JOIN numbered prev ON curr.rn = prev.rn + 1
)
SELECT * FROM consecutive
ORDER BY distance_km DESC
LIMIT 1
